identity.title: An Unbiased ALMA Spectral Survey of the LkCa 15 and MWC 480 Protoplanetary Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present here an overview of such a survey of the protoplanetary disks around the Herbig Ae star MWC 480 and the T Tauri star LkCa 15 in ALMA Band 7

evidence.quote: Right ascension, declination, and distance of each source are from the Gaia DR2 catalog

question.value: What are the molecular inventories of the MWC 480 and LkCa 15 disks from an unbiased Band 7 spectral line survey, and how do they differ?

evidence.quote: Significant differences are observed in the molecular inventories of MWC 480 and LkCa 15, and we discuss how these results may be interpreted in light of the different physical conditions of these two disk systems.
LkCa 15 and MWC 480 were observed in Band 7 during ALMA Cycles 3 $\&$ 4 (project code 2015.1.00657.S).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00226.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00657.S.
spanning $\sim$36 GHz from 275–317 GHz

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Five observed settings of 4 FDM SPWs each, 1920 channels, 975 kHz width (~1 km/s); gaps at 306–310 and 318–322 GHz

evidence.quote: Each spectral setup consisted of 4 Frequency Division Mode (FDM) spectral windows, each with 1920 channels.
resulting in coverage gaps between 306–310 GHz and 318–322 GHz

sensitivity.value: Per-channel rms 1.7–3.9 mJy/beam depending on SPW

evidence.quote: Right ascension, declination, and distance of each source are from the Gaia DR2 catalog

what.value: Prior ALMA observations of 12CO, 13CO, C18O, DCO+, H13CO+ used as template filters

evidence.quote: We use prior observations of $^{12}$CO, $^{13}$CO, C$^{18}$O, DCO$^{+}$, and H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ (cite: Huang_2017) to generate a bank of data-driven template filters

what.value: Disk inclination, PA, stellar and disk parameters in Table 1

pipeline_or_manual.value: Initial calibration by ALMA/NAASC staff; then self-calibration in CASA

evidence.quote: Data was initially calibrated by the ALMA/NAASC staff.
Subsequent self-calibration and imaging of the data were completed using `CASA` 4.3.1.

self_calibration.value: 3 rounds phase-only (100s, 30s, 10s) then one amplitude iteration, on continuum

evidence.quote: Three rounds of phase-only self-calibration on the disk continuum emission were then completed with solution intervals of 100s, 30s, and 10s, followed by one iteration of amplitude self-calibration.
Each of the spectral windows for both sources was imaged with `CLEAN` in CASA 4.3.1, using natural weighting for optimal sensitivity.

weighting_robust.value: Natural for survey cubes; continuum robust −0.5; strong lines (>20σ) Briggs robust 0.5

evidence.quote: with a Briggs robust parameter of -0.5
An identical imaging process was used, but with Briggs weighting and a robust value of 0.5.

masking.value: Elliptical masks: MWC 480 3.5" major axis, i=37, PA=148; LkCa 15 4.5", i=52, PA=60; same in all channels; clean to 4σ

evidence.quote: For MWC 480, the mask had a major axis length of 3.5$''$, inclination of 37$\degree$, and PA of 148$\degree$
They were then `CLEAN`ed down to a threshold of 4$\sigma$
continuum subtracted using the CASA task `uvcontsub` (fit-order = 1)

array_combination.value: Executions of the same setting concatenated before imaging

evidence.quote: When a spectral setting had multiple executions taken, the respective measurement sets for each spectral window were concatenated prior to imaging.

analysis_steps.goal: Image full band and extract disk-integrated spectra

method.value: Natural-weighted CLEAN per SPW with fixed elliptical masks; spectra extracted within masks

evidence.quote: disk-integrated spectra were extracted from the image cubes using the elliptical `CLEAN` masks
They were then `CLEAN`ed down to a threshold of 4$\sigma$

method.value: Apply bank of Keplerian data-driven template filters to continuum-subtracted visibilities, yielding filter impulse response spectra

evidence.quote: The interpolated filter is then convolved with the data, producing a normalized filter impulse response spectrum.

key_parameters.value: templates: 12CO, 13CO, C18O, DCO+, H13CO+, plus H2CO, N2H+, CS from survey

evidence.quote: Filters were also created using strong lines of H$_2$CO, N$_2$H$^+$, and CS imaged from the presently described observations.
All spectral lines that were detected by matched filtering in either disk at greater than 4$\sigma$ significance

analysis_steps.goal: Image individual lines and measure fluxes

method.value: Natural-weighted CLEAN (robust 0.5 for >20σ lines), 1.5 km/s channels, integrate disk spectra over fixed velocity ranges, bootstrap errors

evidence.quote: Fluxes for each transition were determined by integrating these spectra from 2.0 to 9.5 km s$^{-1}$ and 3.5 to 11 km s$^{-1}$ in MWC 480 and LkCa 15, respectively.
repeating this process 10000 times on randomly selected nearby emission-free channels, sampled with replacement

analysis_steps.goal: Compare inventories and derive ring radii and upper limits

method.value: Flux ratios as proxy for abundance; deprojected azimuthal profiles for radii; CH3OH upper limit at assumed Tex

evidence.quote: We therefore use the flux density ratios as a rough proxy for abundance comparisons between the two sources.

assumptions.value: Optically thin emission except CS and N2H+; CH3OH Tex = 25 K

evidence.quote: assuming an excitation temperature of 25 K(cite: Walsh_2016; Carney_2019)

findings_qualitative.value: Species requiring CO freeze-out (N2H+, H2CO) and S-bearing species are brighter toward LkCa 15; hydrocarbons and nitriles brighter toward MWC 480

evidence.quote: Species that require CO freeze-out are enhanced toward LkCa 15
Observed transitions of hydrocarbons and nitriles are brighter toward MWC 480.

claims.hypothesis: Can an unbiased ALMA Band 7 survey reveal new molecules in disks?
claims.experiment: Imaging and matched filtering of 275–317 GHz
claims.finding: Five species first detected in disks

evidence.quote: with 5 species (C$^{34}$S, $^{13}$CS, H$_2$CS, DNC, and C$_2$D) detected for the first time in protoplanetary disks

claims.hypothesis: Do the two disks differ in molecular inventory?
claims.finding: Differences possibly mostly due to temperature

evidence.quote: which may be mostly explained by temperature differences between the disks.

claims.hypothesis: Are COMs present at levels predicted by models?
claims.result: No firm detections; low upper limit

evidence.quote: These observations suggest that chemical models over-produce gas-phase abundances of O-bearing complex species.

why_this_method.value: Matched filtering gives higher SNR and faster line identification

evidence.quote: Matched filtering of the survey using prior observations as templates allowed much faster line identification than a traditional imaging approach

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Lower robust values rejected due to higher noise

evidence.quote: Lower values of robustness produced images with substantially higher noise and thus were not used.

limitations_admitted.value: Flux ratios are only a rough abundance proxy; high-Eu lines biased by temperature

evidence.quote: we cannot directly compare abundances between the two disks

referee_caveats_inferred: Abundance comparisons rely on flux ratios without radiative transfer or excitation modelling
Fixed elliptical masks and integration ranges may bias fluxes
Ring radii from low-resolution data lack stated uncertainties
